thread:
Mia: Nightly retrieval eval (eval-rag-nightly/2026-03-19) flagged a large recall regression for the app_help prompt set. topk=10 recall dropped 0.92 -> 0.61. tagging @raj @oliver :eyes:

Oliver: Which index and model versions were used in that job? Did we change the reranker overnight?

eval-bot: Job eval-rag-nightly/2026-03-19 finished 2026-03-19T07:12Z. Config snapshot:
- index: docs-index-v47
- embed_model: redwood-embed-v3-quant-q4a
- reranker: reranker-v3.1.2
- index-refresh: 2026-03-18T23:30Z

Raj: Confirmed — reranker-v3.1.2 rolled at 2026-03-19T02:45Z (canary -> prod). No index rollbacks.

Jen: I pushed a reranker weight change in the canary earlier (lambda 0.8 -> 0.6) to prioritize BM25 signals for short queries. That went to prod in the v3.1.2 rollout. Not sure if that would cause recall to drop that much though.

Cole: Did we also switch quantized embed variant? redwood-embed-v3-quant-q4a is slightly different kernel/ops than v3-quant. Quant artifacts can change neighbor order.

Mia: Here's a couple of failing examples from the eval (query -> expected doc id -> top1..top5):

``
query: "how do i reset API key for service account"
expected: doc_ah_124
top5: doc_misc_42, doc_auth_9, doc_ah_271, doc_auth_88, doc_misc_13
```

``
query: "billing alert threshold set"
expected: doc_ah_022
top5: doc_ops_5, doc_api_7, doc_misc_3, doc_ops_92, doc_api_21
```

Mia: Note the expected docs are present in index and were top1 in previous nightly (2026-03-18) using redwood-embed-v3-quant and reranker-v3.1.0.

Oliver: Those top5 look semantically off — suggests embedding neighborhood shifted. Can we compute pairwise cosine between v3-quant (yesterday) vs v3-quant-q4a (today) for the failing queries + ground-truth docs?

Cole: Running a quick check locally — early results: for ~60% of failing queries the cosine(dir) between old/new embeddings for the query > 0.18 (large). Document embeddings also moved but less consistently.

Raj: If query embeddings moved that much, reranker weight change could amplify drop. The reranker expects candidate set with high recall; if embed step misses the GT doc, reranker can't recover.

Jen: Reverting the reranker weight is quick. But we should isolate whether quantized embed variant is primary cause before doing that.

Mia: Agreed. Proposed triage plan:
1) Run recall-by-source for the app_help cohort comparing three runs: (A) yesterday config (v3-quant + reranker-v3.1.0), (B) today embed only (v3-quant-q4a + reranker-v3.1.0), (C) today full prod (v3-quant-q4a + reranker-v3.1.2).
2) Diff candidate pools and compute % cases where GT doc drops out of top50.
3) Sanity-check a handful of queries with unquantized embeddings (redwood-embed-v3-fp16) to see if quantization is main factor.

Cole: I'm on step 1B now. Command I'm running:
``
python eval/retrieval/compare_recall.py --cohort app_help --runs "A:cfg/2026-03-18.json" "B:cfg/2026-03-19-embed.json" --topk 50 --out /tmp/recall_diff.json
```

Cole: quick stat from B vs A (top50): GT dropped out in 38% of queries. That's consistent with earlier coarse check.

Mia: 38% is huge. If B vs A accounts for most of the regression, we should prioritize embed rollback or promote alternate quant profile.

Oliver: Can we check embedding dimensionality mismatch or accidental re-normalization? Sometimes quant variants skip final L2 norm.

Cole: Good call. I inspected the embedding pipeline: old flow applies L2 norm after quant-decode; new q4a flow uses in-kernel approximate norm, but result shows vectors are re-normalized. I verified norms distribution:
- old mean norm: 0.9998
- new mean norm: 1.0004
so re-normalization doesn't look broken.

Jen: I can kick a canary revert of reranker weight to 0.8 for the canary subset (10% traffic) to see if it helps recall in production telemetry. Should be low-risk.

Raj: Hold on rollbacks for a sec — if embedding is the root cause, reranker revert will not restore ground truth to candidate set; it might just reorder garbage.

Mia: Agree. Let's prioritize reproducing with unquantized embed model. Cole, can you run 1C_unquant: keep today's reranker but swap embed to redwood-embed-v3-fp16 on the same index snapshot (no reindex)?

Cole: Running now. ETA ~20m. Also exporting example token-level diffs for a failing query to help model/ops team.

[20m passes]

Cole: Results: comparing unquantized vs q4a (both with reranker-v3.1.2): GT missing from top50 in 6% of queries. So quantized variant accounts for most of the delta (38% -> 6%). Still some residual. Raw numbers attached in /tmp/recall_diff.json

Mia: That points to quantization kernel causing neighbor reorder for many queries. Action items:
- Cole: produce a short repro script + failing query list and open infra issue linking q4a kernel and nightly metrics (assign to eng-runtime). ETA 2h.
- Oliver/Raj: hold reranker revert for now; instead disable q4a embed rollout (point nightly and canary back to v3-quant) and re-run nightly job to confirm recovery.
- Jen: stand by for canary reranker revert if disabling embed rollout is not possible quickly.

Oliver: I'll coordinate with infra to gate q4a in the model catalog and publish a rollback flag. Also ping runtime for kernel diagnostics.

Cole: Filed issue infra#2134 with repro, diff artifacts, and example queries. Link: https://redwood.internal/infra/2134

Mia: Thanks all. Re-run scheduled: 2026-03-19T10:00Z after embed rollback. We'll monitor app_help recall and overall RAG eval dashboards: https://console.redwood.ai/evals/nightly

Raj: One more note — add a short automated check in nightly to compare embedding neighborhood stability (cosine drift) between model variants; if mean drift > 0.05, fail the job and alert. This would catch regressions before rollouts.

Oliver: Agreed. I'll add that to the eval harness as a quick metric.

Jen: FYI I saw a couple customer support tickets this morning referencing missing docs in search for billing topics — correlates with the regression window. I'll hold CS updates until we confirm rollback.

Mia: Great. We're aligned. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

Eval-bot: Follow-up job scheduled: eval-rag-nightly/2026-03-19-rollback-check at 2026-03-19T10:05Z
